performance_optimizations.title: Add database indexes for frequently queried columns
performance_optimizations.description: The database schema lacks indexes on columns that are heavily queried with filters and ordering. The images, chatMessages, designs, and chatConversations tables are queried with WHERE clauses on userId, generationType, isFavorite, and LIKE search on prompt, with ORDER BY on createdAt/lastMessageAt/updatedAt. Without indexes, these queries perform full table scans.
performance_optimizations.rationale: Every image gallery load, chat history fetch, designs list, and conversation retrieval currently scans the entire table. With 10,000+ rows per table, queries can take 100-500ms. Adding composite indexes would reduce this to <10ms. This is the highest-impact database optimization available.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: Full table scan on every query (O(n) for n rows)
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: 10-50x faster queries with index lookups (O(log n))
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Add composite index on images(userId, createdAt DESC) for gallery listing
2. Add index on images(userId, isFavorite) for favorites filter
3. Add index on images(userId, generationType) for type filter
4. Add GIN index on designs(tags) for array containment queries
5. Add index on chatConversations(userId, lastMessageAt DESC) for conversation list
6. Add index on chatMessages(conversationId, createdAt) for message retrieval
7. Generate and run migration with Drizzle Kit
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Slight increase in write latency (~1-2ms per INSERT) and storage overhead. Worth it for read-heavy workload pattern.

performance_optimizations.title: Memoize useCanvas() combined hook to prevent cascade re-renders
performance_optimizations.description: The useCanvas() combined hook in src/context/canvas/index.ts creates a new object literal on every call (lines 138-200), aggregating 5 sub-contexts without memoization. This defeats the purpose of the context split architecture and causes all consumers to re-render whenever ANY sub-context changes.
performance_optimizations.rationale: The application correctly split CanvasContext into 5 focused contexts (CanvasStateContext, ElementsContext, LayerContext, HistoryContext, ImageContext). However, the combined useCanvas() hook returns a new object on every render, negating the optimization. Components using useCanvas() will re-render when elements change, even if they only need canvas state. This is visible in App.tsx where useCanvas() is called in VoiceAgentWrapper.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: New object created on every useCanvas() call, cascading re-renders through context tree
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~40-60% reduction in re-renders for canvas-dependent components, smoother canvas interactions
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Complex dependency array for useMemo; migration to specific hooks is cleaner but more invasive

performance_optimizations.title: Implement parallel AI provider fallback with smart timeouts
performance_optimizations.description: The generateImage function in src/services/imageGenerationService.ts uses sequential try/catch fallbacks (Nano Banana Pro -> Flux Schnell -> Flux Dev). Each provider attempt must complete or timeout before the next begins, creating worst-case latencies of 15-30+ seconds when providers are slow or unavailable.
performance_optimizations.rationale: Current sequential approach: if primary times out in 10s, fallback 1 times out in 10s, users wait 20s before fallback 2 even starts. Image generation is the core user flow, and these delays feel broken. Using Promise.any() with staggered starts could resolve with first success while maintaining cost control.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: Sequential fallback: 15-30s worst-case generation time during provider issues
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~60-70% reduction in worst-case generation time; <10s even during partial outages
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Implement tiered parallel strategy with AbortController:
   ```typescript
   const controller = new AbortController();
   const tier1 = tryProvider('nano-banana-pro', controller.signal);
   
   const result = await Promise.any([
     tier1,
     tier1.catch(() => sleep(3000)).then(() => tryProvider('flux-schnell', controller.signal)),
     tier1.catch(() => sleep(6000)).then(() => tryProvider('flux-dev', controller.signal))
   ]);
   
   controller.abort(); // Cancel remaining requests
   ```
2. Track provider health metrics to dynamically adjust tier delays
3. Consider cost implications (parallel requests may increase API spend)
4. Add circuit breaker pattern for repeatedly failing providers
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: May increase API costs if multiple providers are called simultaneously; requires AbortController support in API client

performance_optimizations.title: Move tag filtering from JavaScript to PostgreSQL with GIN index
performance_optimizations.description: The GET /designs endpoint in server/src/routes/designs.ts (lines 37-44) fetches ALL user designs then filters by tags in JavaScript. This wastes database bandwidth and memory, especially as users accumulate designs.
performance_optimizations.rationale: Post-query filtering loads unnecessary data from the database. The code fetches up to 50 designs, then filters in JS: `filteredDesigns = userDesigns.filter(d => d.tags?.some(...))`. PostgreSQL's array operations with GIN indexes are optimized for exactly this use case. Moving filter to SQL leverages query planning and reduces data transfer.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: All designs fetched to memory, then filtered; O(n*m) JS filtering
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~50-80% reduction in data transfer; database handles filtering with O(log n) index lookups
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: PostgreSQL-specific syntax; requires migration deployment; need to ensure tag normalization (lowercase) at write time

performance_optimizations.title: Implement localStorage cleanup and batching for performance metrics
performance_optimizations.description: The trackModelPerformance function in src/services/modelRouter.ts stores up to 1000 metric entries in localStorage (line 23). Each tracked metric triggers a full read-parse-push-write cycle. With heavy usage, this array can reach 200-400KB, causing synchronous localStorage operations to block the main thread.
performance_optimizations.rationale: localStorage is synchronous and blocks the main thread. The performance_log array is read and rewritten on every AI operation. With objects containing timestamps, model IDs, latency, and success rates, 1000 entries creates significant payload. This creates UI jank during the exact moments users are waiting for AI results.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: Synchronous localStorage read/write (200-400KB) on every metric tracked
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: ~70% reduction in localStorage payload; eliminate storage-related UI jank
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Metrics may be lost on hard close before flush; requires migration strategy for existing users
